Hon'ble Manoj Kumar Tiwari, J.
Hon'ble Pankaj Purohit, J.
Ms. Ketki Chaudhary and Mr.
Abhishek Anthwal, learned counsel for the
petitioner.
2. Mr. N.S. Pundir, learned counsel for
respondent no.1/Bank.
3. Mr. B.P.S. Mer, learned Standing
Counsel along with Mr. M.S. Bisht, learned
Brief Holder for the State.
4. Petitioner participated in selection
held by respondent no.2 for appointment as
Officer Scale-II (Treasury). In that selection,
petitioner was declared successful and he
was offered appointment by respondent
no.3, vide letter 30.03.2026. In that letter,
it was mentioned that petitioner will have to
submit all necessary documents with
respondent no.3 by 10.04.2026. Petitioner
was not able to submit the documents
within stipulated time; therefore, he sought
extension of time. Respondent no.3 granted
extension till 13.07.2026, and it was
mentioned in the communication issued by
respondent no.3 that in case petitioner
fails to submit the documents by
13.07.2026, his candidature shall be
deemed to be cancelled. Petitioner,
thereafter, sought another extension vide

UKHC010166922026
2026:UHC:8912-DB
email dated 01.07.2026. The request made
by petitioner for extension of time was
turned down by respondent no.3 by
referring to the stipulation made in the
earlier communication, whereby deadline
was fixed as 13.07.2026. Thus, feeling
aggrieved, petitioner has approached this
Court seeking the following reliefs:-
(a) Issue a writ, order or direction in the nature of
Certiorari quashing the communication/action
dated 13.07.2026 (Annexure No.9) vide which
the candidature of the petitioner was cancelled.
(b) Issue a writ, order or direction in the nature of
mandamus directing the respondents to
reconsider the candidature of the petitioner for the
post of Manager (Treasury) in the light of the Offer
Letter dated 30.03.2026 (Annexure no.1) and the
petitioner's representations/correspondence, and
upon such reconsideration, communicate to the
petitioner a definite date of joining and grant him
a reasonable period to complete the resignation,
NOC and relieving formalities from his existing
employer and thereafter permit him to join, subject
to fulfillment of the applicable terms and
conditions.
5. Learned counsel for petitioner submits
that petitioner is presently employed as
Manager with I.C.I.C.I. Bank and as per the
contract of service, he has to give three
months notice before leaving the present
employment, thus I.C.I.C.I. Bank has not
relieved the petitioner so far.
6. We asked learned counsel for the
petitioner to show us the document
whereby he requested I.C.I.C.I. Bank for
his relieving or for depositing salary for
notice period as per his contract of service
with I.C.I.C.I. Bank, but no such document
was produced, even though, Coordinate
Bench asked the petitioner vide order dated
24.09.2026, to bring on record any

UKHC010166922026
2026:UHC:8912-DB
evidence in that regard.
7. Having regard to the facts and
circumstances of the case, we do not find
any scope of interference, as on petitioner's
request time for submitting documents was
extended by respondent no.3. Respondent
no.3 cannot be asked to wait for indefinite
period as the selection process has
concluded in the month of March, and
there are other candidates, who are waiting
for appointment.
8. Accordingly, the writ petition is
dismissed.

(Pankaj Purohit, J.) (Manoj Kumar Tiwari, J.)
 01.10.2026
Nahid/R.Bisht
